parameters.content:
### How it works
Operations teams that need a searchable document archive for an intake mailbox. Save permitted attachments, independently download and hash every new file, and remember confirmed work across runs. Completed receipts suppress repeats. An uncertain destination result stops processing and holds the lock for manual recovery.

### Setup
Requires Folderit **Tailor with API access**, a dedicated test destination and provider credentials. Install Folderit using the connection guide below. Tested on n8n **2.46.0** with **n8n-nodes-folderit 0.4.0**; Data Table v1.1 is required.

1. Keep inactive. Choose a stable table name in **Ledger setup settings** and run only **1. Set up receipt table**, once at a time in the same n8n project.
2. Connect an IMAP credential in **New email with attachments** and the SAME **Folderit OAuth2 API** credential in all three Folderit actions. Set accountUid, folderUid, mailboxScope and allowedExtensions in **Settings**. mailboxScope is a permanent label for this mailbox, not its password. After the setup branch succeeds, paste its ledgerTableId into Settings. Never put secrets in Settings. Copies processing the same input must share the table.
3. Start with an empty test inbox: existing unseen mail can be fetched. Activate before sending two allowed test attachments and one excluded file. Check downloaded bytes and replay suppression.

### Customization
Change allowedExtensions for your intake. A stable Message-ID is required; empty files and files over 100 MiB fail. Extension filtering is not malware scanning.

[Connection and first-run guide](https://www.folderit.com/knowledge-base/connect-folderit-to-n8n/) · [Recovery instructions](https://github.com/folderit-dms/n8n-nodes-folderit/blob/main/CUSTOMER-WORKFLOWS.md#recovery-inspect-before-retrying)

[Workflow image](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/folderit-dms/n8n-nodes-folderit/main/templates/assets/archive-imap-attachments.png)

## 2 · Select safe attachments
Configure the IMAP and Settings nodes first. Split permitted attachments and hash their bytes; read/unread status is unchanged. Message-ID and attachment identity distinguish repeats from a different email with identical content.

## 3 · Process one item at a time
A shared lock serializes overlapping runs. Confirm ownership before continuing; competing runs wait for about one minute, then stop. There is no automatic lock expiry: a failed run needs inspection.

## 4 · Skip confirmed work
Look up the item’s durable receipt. Completed work follows the upper bypass; a new item continues to the destination action. Pending or inconsistent receipts stop for recovery instead of repeating an uncertain action.

## 5 · Record before uploading
Save a pending receipt before creating the Folderit file. If the request fails or times out, inspect the actual destination before retrying; the file may already exist.

## 6 · Verify the stored bytes
Read the new document, download its stored binary and compare SHA-256 with the original attachment. Only an exact match may become a completed receipt. A successful upload status alone is insufficient.

## 7 · Save the result, then unlock
Confirm the completed receipt before freeing the lock and taking the next item. Retain completed receipts. After a failure, confirm the old owner has stopped and reconcile every pending result before releasing its lock.

## 1 · Run setup before the service trigger
Choose a stable table name, then run this manual branch once. It validates or creates local receipts and the lock without contacting providers. Copy the final ledgerTableId into the main Settings node; preserve this table on upgrades.
